messages:
Anya: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose an explicit transition state machine in the edge proxy to remove ambiguity when we move request ownership midflight. TL;DR: introduce a TRANSFER/DELEGATED flow with a transfer token + attempt_id so retries and billing are deterministic.

Kai: Sketch it out?

Anya: Sketch: STATES = `RECEIVED` -> `STREAMING` -> `TRANSFER` -> `DELEGATED` -> (`COMMITTED` | `ABORTED`). Invariants: single active owner; transfer is only allowed from STREAMING -> TRANSFER and must finish with either DELEGATED (success) or ORPHANED (failed) which triggers reconciliation. Transfer carries TransferToken that contains attempt_id + minimal KV snapshot.

Ben: How does this interact with client-side retries? Double-exec risk is our top worry.

Anya: We bind idempotency_token + attempt_id to the full lifecycle. Retry with same idempotency_token should be deduplicated by upstream if the attempt_id is <= last_committed_attempt. Transfer preserves these tokens. If an upstream can't dedupe, gateway falls back to conservative abort-with-error.

Marta: Observability ask: emit transfer_start, transfer_commit, transfer_orphaned traces + counter for orphaned duration. Need these to detect flakiness quickly.

ops-bot: incident-bot: FYI — a duplicate replay was observed in prod yesterday (see #incidents/3264). This proposal might have prevented it.

Kai: Edge-case: partial-response during transfer — do we stream partial to client and expect resume, or terminate and ask client to replay? My leaning: support resume when client supports it, otherwise terminate with clear trailer.

Anya: Agreed. Protocol additions: add trailer headers `x-transfer-resume: <token>` and `grpc-status: TRANSFER_REQUIRED` when we ask a client to replay. For clients that advertise resume capability we include the token so they can resume from the last committed chunk.

Ben: KV cache consistency is tough. If we transfer, the new owner needs prefix/KV state. Snapshots can be heavy.

Anya: Tradeoffs: small prefix snapshot (configurable N tokens) vs rehydrate-on-demand via deterministic prompt + checkpoint id. Default: snapshot up to 512 tokens; if >512 mark transfer as expensive and either fail transfer or force abort. We'll measure cost delta.

Leah: Migration/ops: make transfer opt-in per route and per cluster. Start with 0.5% traffic, collect metrics (duplicates, transfer_success, transfer_latency), then ramp. Also need feature flag for disabling snapshoting.

Anya: Rollout plan noted. I'll open the PR with the state machine diagram, invariant checks, and proto changes.

Kai: Can you paste a quick proto snippet for TransferToken here so I can do a quick pass?

Anya: Sure — proto sketch:

```proto
message TransferToken {
  string id = 1;
  string attempt_id = 2;
  bytes kv_snapshot = 3;
  map<string,string> meta = 4;
}
```

Ben: Minor but important: billing and rate limits — who consumes capacity during transfer? My vote: source owner continues to consume tokens until transfer_commit; that keeps quotas sane.

Marta: +1 for billing rule. Also add metric `transfer_commit_latency_ms` and `transfer_orphan_duration_ms`.

deploy-bot: created INF-2345: "proxy: transfer state machine proto + rollout checklist"

Anya: :thumbsup: I'll open PR by EOD and attach the rollout checklist + test plan.

Kai: Thanks — will review the proto + invariants once PR is up.

Marta: One more ops note: add a guard that prevents transfer when memory pressure is high; prefer abort so we don't OOM trying to snapshot.

Anya: Good call — will add pressure-based gating and an opt-out annotation for low-latency routes.

Ben: Great thread. If we can get a small POC that flips on for a single internal route, we can validate KV snapshot cost quickly.

Anya: POC plan: internal streaming route -> transfer=on -> 0.5% traffic -> collect metrics. I'll include smoke tests for duplicate suppression and resume tokens.

Leah: Thanks!
